finding: The repair batch made §2's own sentence false, in the same batch. §2 reads: `The five-layer form is still written in CLAUDE.md, which is where this draft copied it from; that is fixed with this release.` Commit 975a1b8 -- one of the four commits that answer round 4 -- rewrote that CLAUDE.md line to `task override > project config > built-in`. Measured now: `CLI > env` returns zero matches in CLAUDE.md. So the present-tense claim `is still written in CLAUDE.md` is false as of the commit that sits beside the sentence asserting it, and `that is fixed with this release` describes a change already committed rather than a deliverable this release ships. §5 has no test for it, and there is nothing left for an implementer to do. This is a self-referential claim about repository state written into a spec that outlives the state -- the class CLAUDE.md's own rule names (`a measured constant in a comment goes stale faster than a release`), and here it went stale before the round it was written for closed.
suggestion: Put the sentence in the past tense and bind it to the artifact rather than to the file's current contents: `An earlier draft of this section wrote the five-layer chain, copied from CLAUDE.md's project-config line; that line was corrected in 975a1b8.` Drop `that is fixed with this release` -- it is not release content.

finding: §2 names CLAUDE.md as the source of the five-layer error and treats correcting it as closing the matter. Two other files still carry the chain, and one of them is in this release's own touch list. Measured: `skills/tp/REFERENCE.md:519-522` states it as THE rule for workflow fields -- `**Resolution (resolve-at-read)** -- effective value per field, highest layer wins:` over a fenced block reading `CLI flag  >  environment  >  task-file workflow override  >  .tp/config.json  >  built-in default`, sitting directly under the workflow-field table that line 505 links to it from. And `spec/0.31.0.md:41`, the shipped spec of `review_converge_on` -- the field §2 calls this one's twin -- reads `It resolves like every other workflow field (CLI > env > task override > project config > built-in default)`. §2's own cost paragraph lists `skills/tp/REFERENCE.md` and `skills/tp/SKILL.md` as surfaces `review_converge_on` touches, so this release will document `audit_converge_on` into a reference whose stated precedence rule contradicts §2's first paragraph. The same file is already internally inconsistent: REFERENCE.md:112 gives `commit_strategy` as `task override > .tp/config.json > built-in default`. Note also that REFERENCE.md:521 is not simply wrong -- `no_color` (line 532) really does have a flag and env layer -- so the fix is a scope qualifier, not a deletion.
suggestion: Add REFERENCE.md:519-522 to §2's scope: the resolution block is qualified to say the flag/environment layers apply to output defaults, not to workflow fields, which resolve `task override > .tp/config.json > built-in`. Note `spec/0.31.0.md:41` as a shipped-spec error left uncorrected, or correct it in the same commit. `CLI > env` in `spec/0.35.0.md:575` is the historical record of the removal and must stay.

Line 241 reads `| 0.37.0 | audit convergence | audit_converge_on, accepted rows stop blocking, a changed spec ends the streak | 287 |`. `accepted rows stop blocking` is Non-Goal 2, moved to spec/0.46.0.md §8.1 by 43f29e8 in this same batch; and the line count is 287 against a file measured at 245 lines (`wc -l spec/0.37.0.md`). Lines 206-208 now read: `spec/0.37.0.md §5 takes the divergence, so **do not re-derive it. **And v0.37.0 does not fix it** -- ...`. §5 of this spec is now `Tests`; the divergence is Non-Goal 1, which hands it to spec/0.46.0.md §8. finding: Round 4's regression row `assertion-on-the-contested-decision-dropped` asked for the built-in default to be restored to test 1; the rewrite changed test 1's precedence chain and left the default out. New test 1: `audit_converge_on resolves task override > project config > built-in, and an invalid value is refused with the same hint shape review_converge_on uses. The mutation that kills it: a resolver reading only the project layer.` The named mutation is about layering; no test in the list of twelve names the built-in VALUE. Measured: the string `default` does not appear in any of §5's twelve entries. §2 states `Default: all`, §2.1 spends a subsection defending it against `blocking`, and §1's `changes nothing for a project that does not set it` is true only if the built-in is `all` -- so an implementation shipping `blocking` as the built-in passes all twelve tests while inverting the release's headline decision and silently relaxing the gate for every existing project. This is the one decision §2.1 exists for and it is the one decision §5 does not pin.
suggestion: Restore it to test 1: `... resolves task override > project config > built-in, with built-in default `all``, and add the corollary §1's no-op claim rests on -- a project that sets nothing records the same clean/converged verdicts as v0.36.0. The mutation that kills it: flipping the built-in constant.

finding: Test 6 replaced old test 5 and kept only half its subject. Old test 5: `Replaying v0.35.0's nine recorded rounds reproduces the §2.1 row -- blocking at 3, all at 9 -- AND replaying v0.36.0's thirteen reproduces blocking at 3 and all never.` New test 6 covers v0.35.0's nine rounds alone. §2.1's table still carries the v0.36.0 row, and it is the load-bearing half: §2.1's decisive argument (`blocking would have shipped over an error row in 2 of 2 measured cycles`) reads `v0.36.0's rounds 7, 12 and 13 each carry error rows`, and the `all` column's `never -- no round reaches zero` is the strongest single number in the section. Nothing now pins either. The drop is also unexplained by test 6's own stated reason: it pins v0.35.0 into `testdata/` precisely because live state moves, and v0.36.0's corpus is the one that is still moving -- CLAUDE.md lists v0.36.0 as `In flight`, and I measured its state.json at 13 audit rounds today, a count that will change with the next recorded round while §2.1 asserts it as a fact.
suggestion: Either extend test 6 to both cycles -- the same testdata copy, the same cited commit, the same two expectations for v0.36.0 -- or state in §2.1 that the v0.36.0 row is illustrative and unpinned because that cycle is in flight, and mark the `13` as measured at a named commit.

The new header (lines 6-13): `v0.37.0 no longer contains that mechanism ... this release's precondition is §8.1, not §3, and nothing schedules it before v0.46.0.` The untouched body, line 48, under the heading `## 3. That is the counting half and it ships first because convergence needs it; this is the durability half.` And line 54, Non-Goal 1: `An accepted finding's blocking behaviour is spec/0.37.0.md §3.` So 0.41.0 now states and denies the same premise in one file, and the surviving half is the normative half -- §3 and Non-Goal 1 are what a decomposer reads to scope the release, while the header is a note. A third pointer in the same untouched block is independently broken: line 55 cites `spec/0.37.0.md Non-Goal 1` as carrying the reasoning for deferring `scope`, and this spec's Non-Goal 1 is the `--check` divergence.

finding: Near-miss, reported per the round's instruction. §4's repair states `internal/cli/audit_signal_test.go`'s guard carries `eleven assert/require calls, counted`, that lines 473-474 are the two reversed, and that `:498` is the streak-entry assertion. I had this queued as an uncounted quantifier, because reversing :473-474 does more than flip two booleans: line 472 is `runTP(t, dir, "set", "--workflow", "--project", "audit_converge_on=blocking")`, so once the field ships that call stops failing and WRITES blocking into the fixture's project config before the remaining nine assertions run -- and three of them (:485-487 role_streaks open 1, :490 --check exits 1) measure exactly what that knob changes. Verified instead of assumed. Counted eleven assert/require calls in lines 469-503; :473-474 are the unknown-field pair; :498 is `assert.Len(t, e, 3, ...)`. The nine do stand, and the reason is worth stating: `signalRow` (audit_signal_test.go:40-42) emits `{item_id, role, status}` with NO severity key, which is §5 test 5's case (c), so §2's fail-closed rule counts go-safety's FAIL as blocking and the round stays unclean. The wrong conclusion would have been to file the quantifier as unverified. The right observation is narrower: nine assertions that were independent of `audit_converge_on` become dependent on §2's fail-closed rule the moment the field ships.
suggestion: Add one clause to §4: the nine stand because the fixture's rows carry no severity and §2's fail-closed rule therefore keeps the round unclean under `blocking` -- so a unit that implements the fence but not the fail-closed rule breaks three of the nine, not zero.
